ORDER These miscellaneous appeals under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 are filed by the claimants being aggrieved of the award dated 27.10.2016 passed by the learned 15th Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Bhopal in MCC No.1257/2015 (Vali Singh Vs. Ishu Parihar and others), MCC No.1252/2015 (Banti Vs. Ishu Parihar and others), MCC No.1258/2015 (Maniram Lodhi Vs. Ishu Parihar and others) and MCC No.1260/2015 (Sahab Singh Vs. Ishu Parihar and others).

sentences.text: 2. Shri Rakesh Jain, learned counsel is appearing for the insurance company in three cases.
Nobody is appearing for the respondent-insurance company in case of Maniram Lodhi.

Vali Singh vs Ishu Parihar on 18 December, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/152992795/
3
3. Shri Rakesh Kumar Jain, learned counsel appearing for the appellants- claimants submits that Vali Singh had sustained fracture of right femur bone and fracture of ribs.
It is submitted that accident took place on 07.12.2014.

Despite certificate of the doctor that Sahab Singh had sustained 30% permanent disability, still Tribunal has awarded only meager compensation of Rs.5,000/- to each of the appellants, namely, Banti, Sahab Singh and Maniram Lodhi.

4. It is pointed out that as far as claimant Banti is concerned, according to Pre MLC (Ex.P-5), Banti Rajak S/o Mulayam Singh was examined by Dr. B.T. Chaturvedi, Medical Officer, CHC, Pichhore (Shivpuri), where he had found multiple contusions on back Red 20 X 18 cm area.
Contusion on left knee 15 X 6 cm Red.
Multiple abrasion on thigh 20 X 7 cm (Red).
All the injuries are caused by hard and blunt objects.

Therefore, looking to the nature of injuries, award of Rs.5,000/- is enhanced to Rs.10,000/- as trauma is apparent from the medical report (Ex.P-5), which has not been disputed and for Trauma a sum of Rs.10,000/- will meet the ends of justice.

Thus, there will be enhancement to the tune of Rs.5,000/- (Rupees Five Thousand only) in favour of the claimant- appellant Banti which will earn interest @ 6% from the date of filing of the claim petition till the date of actual payment.
Other terms and conditions of the award shall remain intact.
5. As far as claimant Sahab Singh is concerned, in his MLC (Ex.P-88), it is mentioned that no laceration/bleeding/clot found on both sides.
No tenderness/bleeding was found.
There was laceration of lower lip involving mucosa.
In the mandible, no tenderness was found and then treatment is mentioned.
In Ex.P-89, Dr. B.T. Chaturvedi observed laceration on lower lip with 5 X 2-1/2 cm wound.
Then multiple abrasion on whole face reddish caused by hard and blunt object.
Contusion 10 X 6 cm on right knee (Red) caused by hard and blunt object.
Contusion 12 X 5 cm on left knee (Red) caused by hard and blunt object.
Lacerated wound 5 X 2 cm bleeding on scalp left parietal area caused by hard and blunt object.

6. Dr. P.S. Thakur has issued Disability Certificate in favour of claimant Sahab Singh, certifying 30%
disability.
Dr. P.S. Thakur claims himself to be Medical Officer, M.S. (Orthopedics), District Government Hospital, Hoshangabad (M.P.).
Admittedly, there was no fracture on the left knee.
Issuance of certificate by a single doctor without getting it endorsed from the District Medical Board, is a serious issue.
Dr. Pushpraj Singh Thakur is examined as claimant witness.
He has deposed about Sahab Singh that he had issued Disability Certificate (Ex.P-90) which contains his signatures from 'A' to 'A' part and signatures of the patient are from 'B' to 'B' part.
He has certified that there was stiffness in his knee joint and, therefore, he has certified 30% disability.
He could not give details as to on which basis he has certified 30% disability to Sahab Singh.
This is a serious matter.

7. Matter be referred to the Principal Secretary, Public Health and Family Welfare Department to take action against Dr. Pushpraj Singh Thakur for giving such certificate without there being any scientific basis to issue the same and also to seek his explanation that why certificates are being issued, without patients being referred to the District Medical Board, which is competent to issue such medical certificates.

4 8.
Therefore, looking to the total facts and circumstances of the case and looking to the nature of injuries, award of Rs.5,000/- is enhanced to Rs.10,000/- , which will meet the ends of justice.

Thus,
there will be enhancement to the tune of Rs.5,000/- (Rupees Five Thousand only) in favour of the claimant-appellant Sahab Singh which will earn interest @ 6% from the date of filing of the claim petition till the date of actual payment.
Other terms and conditions of the award shall remain intact.

9. As far as appellant-claimant Maniram Lodhi is concerned, in the pre MLC (Ex.P-10) of Maniram Lodhi as was carried out by Dr. B.T. Chaturvedi, it is mentioned that there was multiple injuries (contusion) (Red) 25 X 8 cm area on back.
There was multiple abrasion on chest Red 10 X 10 cm area.
All the injuries were caused by hard and blunt object.
There is no history of any fracture or hospitalization.
10. In view of such facts and looking to the nature of injuries, award of Rs.5,000/- is enhanced to Rs.10,000/-, which will meet the ends of justice.

Thus, there will be enhancement to the tune of Rs.5,000/- (Rupees Five Thousand only) in favour of the claimant-appellant Maniram Lodhi which will earn interest @ 6% from the date of filing of the claim petition till the date of actual payment.
Other terms and conditions of the award shall remain intact.
11. As far as appellant-claimant Vali Singh is concerned, admittedly he sustained fracture of right femur bone and ribs.

Tribunal has awarded only a sum of Rs.20,000/- under the head of Pain &
Suffering.
Looking to the multiple fractures, this amount is enhanced to a sum of Rs.50,000/-.

Thus,
there will be enhancement to the tune of Rs.30,000/- under the head of Pain & Suffering.
12. As far as award of amount under the head of Transport, Special Diet and Attendant is concerned

,
Tribunal has awarded only a sum of Rs.3,000/-.
Looking to the nature of fracture and the period of recuperation, a sum of Rs.16,000/- is awarded at the rate of Rs.4,000/- per month for a period of four months under the head of Nutritious Diet.
Similarly, another sum of Rs.16,000/- is awarded at the rate of Rs.4,000/- per month for a period of four months under the head of Attendant.

Tribunal has awarded only a sum of Rs.3,000/- cumulatively under the head of Transport but looking to the fact that Treatment was taken by the claimant not only at Pichhore but also at Jhansi and Bhopal too, a sum of Rs.15,000/- is awarded under the head of Transport.
Thus, there will be enhancement to the tune of Rs.12,000/- under the head of Transport.

13. Tribunal has awarded only a sum of Rs.6,000/- under the head of Loss of Earning, whereas looking to the fact that accident took place on 07.12.2014, when minimum wages even for an unskilled labourer were to the tune of Rs.6,000/- per month.
Therefore, claimant will be entitled for a sum of Rs.24,000/- for Loss of Earning Capacity against a sum of Rs.6,000/-.
Thus, there will be enhancement to the tune of Rs.18,000/- under this head.
Learned Tribunal has not awarded any amount under the head of Future Treatment, Physiotherapy, etc. for which another sum of Rs.20,000/- is awarded, which will meet the ends of justice.

14. Thus, there will be enhancement to the tune of Rs.1,12,000/- (Rupees One Lakh and Twelve Thousand only) in favour of the claimant-appellant Vali Singh which will earn interest @ 6% from the date of filing of the claim petition till the date of actual payment.

5
the award shall remain intact.
15. In above terms, these miscellaneous appeals are disposed of.
16. Record of the learned Claims Tribunal be sent back.
Later on Shri Gulab Chand Sohane, learned counsel appears and prays for marking his presence for the respondent No.3-insurance company in M.A. No.1196/2017.
On his request, his presence is marked.
